title: GC in one screen
rememberThis: Value types live inline (stack or inside a heap object); reference types are heap objects plus a reference.
Gen 0 is nursery. LOH is ~85,000 bytes and is collected with gen 2; POH holds pinned objects since .NET 5.
ArrayPool and MemoryPool reuse large buffers — Return in finally to avoid LOH churn.
Dispose unmanaged and pooled resources yourself. Finalizers are a last-chance queue on another thread.
Kestrel microservices want server GC + DATAS; containers set heap hard limits — never GC.Collect in request code.
bullets: Roots: stack slots, statics, GCHandles, finalizer queue.
SkiaSharp SKBitmap and similar native wrappers must be in using / await using.
Closures, boxing, string.concat, and materializing LINQ are the usual gen-0 storms — measure alloc-rate.
Pin with GCHandle for interop; Free in finally. WeakReference for caches that yield to GC.
V8 is generational too, but it has no server-GC mode and no LOH threshold you tune the same way.

rows.label: SOH
rows.value: Objects under the LOH threshold, generations 0–2

rows.label: LOH
rows.value: Large arrays ~85 KB+; gen 2 collection; CompactOnce defragments

rows.label: ArrayPool
rows.value: Rent/Return large buffers to avoid per-request LOH alloc

rows.label: Server GC
rows.value: One heap per processor; throughput for services; default on ASP.NET Core

rows.label: DATAS
rows.value: Dynamic heap sizing for variable-traffic microservices
